worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(\frac{\pi }{4},1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & ={sec}^{2}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\ {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(\frac{\pi }{4},1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(1,\frac{\pi }{4})$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
